1

Details

Question (Dylan, 14 Oct): as a proof of concept for LNL or another facility, does the scintillator stack measure energy? Just the SiPM wall and the plastic. Answer it with an internal cross-check, not with the n_TOF physics.

The test: calibrate each layer once, on cosmic muons (a MIP in 3 mm and in 20 mm of PVT, run_149, beam off), and then predict a different population — the beam's 1–7 MeV Compton and pair electrons — with no further tuning. Geant4 provides the prediction for both layers jointly. If the calibrations transfer, Geant4 needs no rescaling.

Data: every gated single MM track ≥ 12 ms after the flash whose own arm fired the trigger, chambers A and C, production runs (all after the 23 July DREAM change). Geant4: the 10⁹-neutron thermal campaign (97 of 100 files), re-reduced for total scintillator deposits per strip and bar (MX17_Full_Geant/scripts/stack_edep.py, condor 4453978), and 1 GeV muon guns for the anchors (condor 4454427).

Verdict in one line: the method works (scale transfers from muons to stopping electrons, linear, stable); the problems it found are one channel (C1) and a rate effect on the PMTs, both identifiable and both things a facility set-up should monitor.

2

Details

Why this is a real test. A muon is minimum-ionising and crosses both layers. The beam electrons are different: 1–7 MeV, mostly stopping in the plastic, entering at an angle, often with their own delta rays and bremsstrahlung in the same counter. If either layer's light output were non-linear, position-dependent or mis-calibrated, the muon-calibrated energies would disagree with Geant4's prediction for the electrons.

Anchoring. The fitter reports the Landau component's peak with the Landau width fixed, and that number moves with the Gaussian smearing (+2–3 % on the wall from Geant4's bare width to the data's). So each counter's MeV anchor is Geant4's 1 GeV muons, smeared until the same fitter returns that counter's measured σ/MPV, and then fitted: wall A 0.471, C 0.473, D 0.474 MeV; plastic A1 3.455, A2 3.458, C1 3.453, C2 3.458, D1 3.445, D2 3.453 MeV. Unsmeared Geant4 muons give 0.462 / 3.398 MeV, i.e. Bichsel's values; the 0.475 / 3.349 of analysis/mip_2cm are another definition.

Geant4 selection, matched to the data: one lepton crossing ≥ 20 mm of the arm's gap, the arm's own trigger (wall group sum ≥ its threshold AND a plastic bar ≥ its threshold) applied to the smeared deposits in MeV, using the thresholds measured in mV and converted with the same calibrations.

3

Details

Fit. Unbinned Landau ⊗ Gauss with a per-event lower truncation where the arm's own trigger needed the wall (landau.fit_trunc), the Landau width fixed at ξ/Δp = 0.056 for 3 mm PVT, the Gaussian free (photostatistics, the light-collection U-shape, path spread). Thresholds sit at ~0.55 of the peak, so the truncation barely matters (truncated fraction < 3 %).

Along the bars each end's response changes by ±25 % (attenuation), but their sum varies by 7 % (half-range) and is highest near the bar ends — a mild U-shape that the sum keeps in the resolution. The geometric mean would cancel attenuation exactly; the sum is used because it is what the hardware discriminates.

Arm B has too few cosmic tracks (42) and is left out, as in C1.

4

Details

Nothing is corrected run by run: the cosmic calibration from run_149 (beam off, after the last beam run) is applied to every run. The plastic median moves by 0.5–0.6 % rms and the wall by 0.8 % rms over 25 runs from run_86 (23 July onwards) to run_162. Part of that is the beam itself (population), so the gain stability is at least this good.

All these runs are on the noisy side of the 23 July DREAM change (CLAUDE.md), as is the calibration run.

5

Details

What is plotted. Data: the larger of the two bars, mV → MeV with that bar's cosmic MIP (C1) and the matched Geant4 anchor. Geant4: the TOTAL prompt deposit in the geometrically matched bar (the lepton, its delta rays, its bremsstrahlung and anything else of the event in that bar), smeared with the bar's measured σ/MPV × √(E·MIP), the arm's trigger applied in MeV. Geant4 is drawn at scale 1: no refit.

The scales (Geant4 × s matches the data's mean over 3–8 MeV; bootstrap errors): see the next slide. Pooling both bars of an arm and all times: A 1.039 ± 0.008, C 1.079 ± 0.013.

What it tests. Most of these electrons STOP in the plastic (below ~6 MeV), so their deposit is their energy, not a dE/dx. Agreement says the light output is linear from the muon's 3.4 MeV (path-normalised) to the stopping electrons' 3–8 MeV, and the scale is the same for a through-going and a stopping particle.

Plastic thickness. A 25 mm bar (the run-config text) would make a muon deposit 4.30 MeV, not 3.40: the data energies would all rise by ×1.27 against a 20 mm Geant4, which three bars at 1.02–1.05 do not allow. The 20 mm of the Geant4 geometry is right (a caliper would close it).

Not included: Birks quenching (Geant4 scores energy, the bars make light). For electrons that stop, the dense end of the track is quenched relative to a MIP, which would make data read LOW by a few %; the data read high, so quenching is not what is being seen.

6

Details

Which Geant4 bar is which. Pinned on A: the data's bar-1/bar-2 ratio is 1.06 at every quantile, as is Geant4's left/right; A's bars sit at different distances from the source, so their spectra differ by that much. C faces A, so its left and right mirror: Geant4's left is C's softer bar, as data bar 2 is.

C1. The C ratio is flat in energy (a pure scale, not a non-linearity) at ~1.12 against Geant4's ~1.06, and C1 alone sits 15 % above Geant4 (its shape also disagrees at low energy: KS p 0.001). Its muon calibration (C1 in the 8 Oct work, ±4 %) and the source calibration agree on C1/C2 to 3 %, so the channel answers electrons differently from muons and sources. Not resolved; candidates: a light-collection or PMT-coupling difference that matters for the electrons' depth and position profile (they stop near the front face, on the bar's inner half), or a gain step between run_149 and the beam runs on that tube alone.

Face maps. The response across each bar, from the electrons' predicted crossings, is flat to ~5 % (face_map.csv), but those crossings are smeared by ~50 mm of scattering, so a sharper non-uniformity is not excluded.

The plastic PMTs lose 3–8 % gain at high rate after the flash; the SiPM wall moves < 2 %

median plastic and wall energy of the self-triggered electrons vs time since the flash, each normalised to its own plateau

A plastic (thick bar 1, thin bar 2)

C plastic

wall, dotted (A, C)

7

Details

From 12–15 ms to the plateau after ~40 ms the plastic median rises by 3 % (A) and 5–8 % (C); the wall moves the other way by 1–2 %. The electron population is the same at all these times (late capture γs), so this is the PMTs' gain recovering as the rate after the flash falls — the effect C1.4 saw on 8 Oct, now measured per bar. The cosmic calibration is at zero rate, so the comparison with Geant4 uses the plateau.

For a facility set-up: a rate-dependent PMT gain is a known effect with known cures (tapered or active bases, lower gain with more amplification after the tube, an LED/pulser monitor through the run).

The wall reads beam electrons at 0.95 of Geant4 in both arms; the shape agrees

same events, plastic ≥ 3 MeV · the wall group with the largest sum · Geant4 smeared by 7 % (A) / 13 % (C) at the MIP, fitted · shown × the fitted scale

data

Geant4 × scale, with the fitted smearing

8

Details

The scale. A 0.951 ± 0.007, C 0.958 ± 0.008 (bootstrap), the same on the rate-free plateau (next to it on the per-bar slide). It does not depend on the smearing (the same to 0.003 over the whole scan, wall_res_scan.csv).

The smearing. The muon fit's Gaussian (σ/MPV ≈ 0.16–0.18) cannot be applied to Geant4 for a 3 mm layer: with the Landau width fixed at ξ it also absorbs the real straggling beyond a Landau, which Geant4 already simulates, and on the cosmics it also carries the path-correction error. Applied anyway, Geant4 comes out too wide (KS p ≤ 0.006; A 0.951, C 0.960). Fitted on the beam electrons instead, the extra smearing is 7 % (A) and 13 % (C) at one MIP, σ ∝ √E — photostatistics plus the light collection along the bar — and the shapes agree (KS p = 0.20 / 0.16).

The ~5 %. The same in both arms, at all times after the flash, and both halves of the wall see it. Candidates: Geant4's thin-layer straggling vs the real one (the anchor carries Geant4's own), a few % of SiPM non-linearity between a muon at normal incidence and electrons at the median angle, or the group sum collecting less of a neighbour's light in the data. It is at the level of the method's own systematics and does not change how the wall is used (a dE/dx tag).

Wall against plastic: flat, as for minimum-ionising electrons, in data and Geant4 alike

median and 16–84 % band of the wall energy in bins of plastic energy · lines: data (colour), Geant4 (ink)

The wall does not measure an electron's energy: from 1 to 7 MeV an electron loses about the same 0.5 MeV in 3 mm. It measures dE/dx (one MIP vs two), and the plastic measures the energy. Both behave as predicted.

9

Details

This is the "estimate in one, compare with the other" test in the form physics allows. Electrons from 1 to 7 MeV are close to minimum-ionising (collision dE/dx in PVT changes by < 5 % over that range), so the wall deposit should not follow the plastic energy. It does not, in either arm, and the slight rise at the lowest plastic energies (slower, more steeply entering electrons) is in both.

For LNL this is the useful division of labour: the thin layer tags MIP vs 2-MIP (an unresolved pair or a conversion in front of the stack) and the thick layer measures the energy of what stops in it.

The scintillator calorimetry worked; two things to fix before relying on it

what the data show

  • Plastic: a muon calibration predicts 3–8 MeV stopping electrons in A1, A2 and C2 at 1.05, 1.03 and 1.02 of Geant4, linear, shapes agreeing.
  • Wall: a clean MIP peak, linear in path; electrons at 0.95 / 0.96 of Geant4, shapes agreeing; it measures dE/dx, as it should.
  • Stable to < 1 % over the campaign with one calibration; the plastic is 20 mm.
  • For LNL: this stack works as an energy measurement for what stops in the plastic, and as a dE/dx tag in the wall.

what to fix, and what this does not rule out

  • Bar C1 reads 1.15 of Geant4 for electrons while muons and sources calibrate it: unexplained, channel-specific.
  • PMT gain sags 3–8 % in the 25 ms after the flash: needs a rate-proof base or a pulser monitor.
  • Muons alone set the scale: add an in-situ electron reference (e.g. a conversion-electron source) per channel at the next facility.
  • Only 3–8 MeV tested (the trigger sets the floor); and the 8 Oct lesson stands: ~1.2 MeV is lost before the plastic.
